subject: Order form: package rebalance and floor-smoothing language
messages:
From: Evan Lowe <evan@acmecloud.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: AcmeCloud Procurement <procurement@acmecloud.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Order form — request to soften stabilizer / floor language

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the updated order form. We reviewed the pricing exhibit and legal has a concern about the current "stabilizer" clause (section Exhibit B, pricing schedule) that effectively locks a hard floor across the SKU bands. For our budgeting model we need more flexibility during the first 6 months of the committed term — particularly for the pilot and initial scale months.

Two specific asks:
- Can Redwood add a temporary pilot carve-out (first 180 days) where the floor is replaced with a lower soft threshold that true-ups at the first annual true-up?
- Can you provide an alternative phrasing that ties the stabilizer to actual consumption buckets rather than calendar months (we prefer a usage-triggered step-in).

I've attached our annotated copy (ACME_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf) and a quick pricing worksheet that shows the sensitivity. We're not asking for price movement — just an operational smoothing so our CFO doesn't have a surprise P&L hit in Q1.

If we can agree on a short snippet that legal is happy with, we can move to signature quickly (we're still on track for a Jan 1 start).

Appreciate your help —
Evan

--
Evan Lowe
Head of Cloud Procurement | AcmeCloud
procurement@acmecloud.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Evan Lowe <evan@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order form — request to soften stabilizer / floor language

Evan —

Thanks for the clear note and the attachments. I pulled in Marissa (who owns the deal) and Ben from pricing. High level: we can be flexible on language for a pilot carve-out, but we need clarity so the stabilizer doesn't get used to materially downgrade the economics post-commit.

Proposed approach:
1) Pilot carve-out: a 180-day window where the floor is reduced to a pilot threshold (example: 50% of the stated floor) and any shortfall is tracked and added to the first true-up. No permanent repricing, just carried-forward true-up.
2) Usage-triggered step-in: replace the current calendar-based trigger with a usage bucket definition. This needs a clean mapping in the order schedule so both sides can compute it deterministically.

I'm attaching a short text snippet with our suggested wording (proposed-stabilizer-snippet.txt) and an updated worksheet showing the accounting treatment. Can you confirm Acme can accept a tracked true-up carried to the first annual true-up (not amortized away)? If yes, we'll have legal prepare a clean redline.

If helpful, we can jump on a 20-minute call early next week to align and get this over the finish line.

Thanks —
Karthik
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Lowe <evan@acmecloud.com>
Date: Sat, 04 Dec 2026 08:43:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order form — request to soften stabilizer / floor language

Adding some pragmatic guardrails from our side — Evan, thanks for the worksheet, that was helpful. A few items from Commercial/Legal POV:

- We agree to the 180-day pilot carve-out but need a firm cap on cumulative carry-forward exposure (proposal: cap carry-forward at 20% of the first year's committed spend). That protects our capacity planning and prevents outsized exposure if usage was accidentally low.
- For the usage-triggered language, let's tie buckets to the monthly rolling 30-day compute units (we can define in an Appendix). That keeps measurement objective.
- We will not accept a permanent discount reprice in the carve-out; the remedy is only a true-up.

Ben, can you confirm whether the 20% cap is feasible from a pricing risk perspective? If not, propose an alternate cap number.

If we can land on the cap + measurement, I'll ask Legal to produce a redline later today. Karthik — happy to host the 20 min call Monday 9am PT if that works for Acme.

Cheers,
Marissa
VP, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Lowe <evan@acmecloud.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order form — request to soften stabilizer / floor language

Marissa / Karthik —

20% cap is acceptable as a commercial compromise for a customer of Acme's scale, but I'd like to offer an alternative that reduces back-office reconciliation: instead of a percentage cap, we propose a fixed-collar approach for the first 180 days — i.e., floor is reduced to X and ceiling remains unchanged, and any delta is recovered at the first annual true-up without carry-forward beyond the collar.

Pros: simpler to explain to finance teams and easier to implement in billing pipelines. Cons: less perfectly aligned to spend if usage plummets.

Suggested numbers (for discussion):
- Pilot floor = 50% of standard floor
- Collar recovery = recover up to 25% of first-year committed value via true-up (hard cap)

If Acme prefers the percentage cap, we'll accept 20%. If they want the collar, we can supply exact dollar amounts in the order schedule.

I'll let you two take this to Evan as a clean option set.

—Ben
Head of Pricing & Packaging
Redwood Inference

From: Evan Lowe <evan@acmecloud.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, AcmeCloud Procurement <procurement@acmecloud.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order form — request to soften stabilizer / floor language

Karthik / Marissa / Ben —

Thanks for the quick turn. We discussed both options with our CFO and procurement. We prefer the fixed-collar approach for operational simplicity — please proceed with the collar language. Two quick asks before legal redline:

1) Can Redwood provide an example numeric collar in the order schedule (we're fine with placeholders but want to see the mechanism)?
2) For the pilot carve-out, can we add a one-time waiver for usage shortfalls tied to a controlled pilot cohort (up to 3 small accounts) so our product team can test without immediate true-up exposure? This would be limited and explicitly enumerated in the appendix.

If you can drop a clean redline with those placeholders (and the DocuSign link ready), we'll route to internal legal and aim to sign within 48 hours.

Appreciate the flexibility — looking forward to closing.

Best,
Evan
--
Evan Lowe
Head of Cloud Procurement | AcmeCloud
